dict.string: Managed settings for cmux (every channel). Keys are cmux.json key paths; capitalized keys are policy keys. Forced values lock the setting; non-forced values replace its default. Exception: agents.chats.roots adds locked roots to the user list; agents.chats.enabled and agents.chats.discovery can only be forced off.
Lists finished shell commands in History. Command lines can contain secrets.
What Go Back and Go Forward walk: places in this workspace, in this window, or the focused page's own history.
Workspaces: Go Back and Go Forward move between workspaces and top pages, and return to the tab each one last had focused. Everything: they also step through tabs and panes inside a workspace.
Each machine deletes recorded commands that are older.
Each machine deletes its oldest closed tabs, screens, workspaces and windows past this many. 0 keeps them all.
Each machine deletes closed items that are older. 0 keeps them however old they are.
Minimal has no titlebar strip; the top row moves the window.
With the sidebar hidden, On Hover hides the sidebar button, Back and Forward until the pointer is over the top row. With the sidebar open, they always show.
Show/Hide All Windows (⌃⌥⌘.) works while another app is in front.
Start Agent (⌃⌥⌘Space) works while another app is in front. Change its key in Keyboard Shortcuts.
cmux keeps running in the menu bar, out of the Dock and the app switcher, until a window opens.
Hide Dock Icon When No Windows Are Open
A cmux item in the menu bar: open cmux, your account, working agents, help, Discord, updates, logs and Quit.
The layout of the New Tab page. Terminal skips the page and opens a terminal. The dots at the bottom of the page also change it.

Cmd-T and the + button open the native New Tab page instead of the web one. It opens faster and lists every command palette action as you type. Recent chats and widgets are only on the web page for now.
Where Cmd-T and the + button put the new tab. New Tab to the Right in a tab's menu always puts it after that tab.
On Hover shows each tab bar's + only while the pointer is over that tab bar.
Where each pane's tab bar sits. At the bottom, the panes reach the top of the window; the window buttons never cover a pane.
Where the address bar row of browser and Markdown panes sits. At the bottom, its suggestions and menus open upward.
In a browser pane with the tab bar and the address bar on the same edge: the tab bar above the address bar, or below it.
Actions shown as buttons next to the tab bar's More button. The rest are in the More menu, where Show in Tab Bar pins them back.
Text size of tab titles. Unset, tabs follow the interface size.
Height of a pane's tab bar. Its tabs grow and shrink with it.
Shrink narrows every tab to the minimum width before the strip scrolls. Scroll keeps tabs wide and scrolls sooner.
Widest a tab gets when the strip has room.
When the strip is crowded, every tab shrinks evenly to this width, and the selected tab stays at least this wide.
Narrowest the other tabs get before the strip scrolls. Never wider than the selected tab's minimum.
Create a new workspace in the current space instead of a tab. Hold Option to reverse this for one click.
When off, Cmd-W on a pinned tab selects the next tab and keeps the pinned tab. Close a pinned tab from its menu.
When on, Cmd-T opens a workspace in the current group and Cmd-N opens a tab. When off, Cmd-T opens a tab, or a workspace when an agent chat or a pane without tabs is focused.
Warn Before Closing a Running Program
Warn Before Closing a Working Agent
Terminals run in cmux-tui and keep running after cmux quits unless you end them.
A share of the window width, for Fixed Width new columns.
A thin bar under the columns that shows and moves the visible range.
Which pane gets focus when the focused pane closes.
Hold Command or Control for 0.30 seconds to show shortcut hints.
Show Shortcuts When Holding a Modifier
Canary and Dev get builds before they reach Nightly. Stable gets only builds that have run a week without problems, so switching to it may mean no updates for a while.
Off: cmux checks for updates and asks before it downloads one. On: updates download by themselves. Either way, cmux asks before it restarts into an update.
While downloads wait, a found update shows on Settings and one click downloads it.
Every Merge: changes to the web UI arrive minutes after they land, without waiting for the next app update. Off: the web UI this app shipped with.
A downloaded update installs as cmux quits. Terminals keep running.
Earlier builds kept so you can roll back. Uses almost no disk until files change.
After an update, a card at the bottom of the sidebar links to What's New until you open or dismiss it.
Now and then, a small tip points at a feature an update added. Close it or use the feature and it never comes back.
A downloaded nightly installs by itself once agents and commands finish and you stop typing, and never waits longer than this. Terminals and agents carry on after the restart.
How long the keyboard and mouse must be idle before a downloaded nightly installs by itself.
Short cards from the cmux team above Settings, shown when the pointer is over the sidebar.
Off: cmux never asks the network for announcements. The request carries no identifiers.
Lets agents see and use your apps through the signed cmux Computer Use helper. macOS asks for Accessibility and Screen Recording when you first allow them.
Legacy runs the current cmux Computer Use helper. Upstream runs the new helper built on the upstream Cua Driver; macOS asks for its permissions separately.
While an agent uses an app, its chat shows a small live view of that app. Click the view to open Agent Activity.
Lets agents use the free cmux AI model while you are signed out. The first time an agent uses it, cmux proves to the Cloud service that this is a real Mac. Sign in for more models and higher limits.
Stops idle sleep while an agent on this Mac is working. Your display can still turn off, and closing the lid still puts the Mac to sleep.
Keep Mac Awake While Agents Work
Terminal agents reopen their session after a crash or restart.
Off, cmux won't switch an agent into a mode that skips approvals.
Agents can suggest next tasks, which you start as child chats beside the current one. Agents started after the change get it.

So your phone can find this Mac, cmux registers with its servers this Mac's name, device ID and platform, the app's bundle ID, version and build channel, the Mac's relay address and connection key, and your account and team IDs. Workspace names, folders, full paths and terminal output go only over the encrypted link to your phone. None of that, and no branch name or repo URL, is sent to cmux servers. Exception: while “Show This Mac's Workspaces on Your Phone While It's Off” is on, cmux servers store each workspace's ID, resource ID, short ID, name, name revision, group, color, icon, pinned state, unread mark, unread count and whether it is active.
Let Your Phone Use This Mac
Off, your phone can still follow, type into and answer what's already running.
Let Your Phone Start New Workspaces
A sleeping Mac can't be reached from your phone until it wakes. Closing the lid still puts the Mac to sleep.
Keep Mac Awake for Your Phone

cmux stores this Mac's workspace names, colors and unread counts so your phone can show them while the Mac is off. A workspace name can be a folder's name. No paths, tab titles or terminal output. Turning this off deletes the copy.
Show This Mac's Workspaces on Your Phone While It's Off

The color of each machine's sidebar rows and tab badges, by machine name: "#RRGGBB", or an accent name (red, green, yellow, purple, cyan, orange, pink, blue) that follows the theme. A machine without one gets a color from its name.
An ssh:// link from another app connects to these hosts without asking. Remove a host to be asked again. Saved machines and acpmux peers never ask.
Each new workspace (Cmd-N, the sidebar's +) gets its own new Cloud machine. Agent chats you start in it run on that machine.
Current Folder copies the folder you work in (its whole git working copy) to the new machine. Empty Folder starts in the machine's own empty folder.
An agent can start other agent sessions to work on parts of a task in parallel. They show under its session in the sidebar.
When an agent in a sub-session asks a question, the session that started it can answer, and the answer shows who gave it. Permission requests always wait for you. Off: only you answer.
Let Sessions Answer Their Sub-sessions' Questions
The most live sub-sessions one session can have at the same time. Running, waiting and harness-alive children count; finished, dead and closed children do not use a slot.
The most sub-sessions one session runs at the same time. More wait their turn and start as running ones finish. Running ones are never stopped when you lower it.
How many levels of sub-sessions can start under a session. 1 lets a session start sub-sessions that cannot start their own.
Agents start in folders under your project roots, and in repositories owned by your organizations, without asking. Other folders ask first.
Trust My Own Folders Without Asking
Everything inside these folders is trusted. Use full paths or ~/ paths.
A repository is trusted when all of its GitHub remotes belong to these users or organizations.
Lets the cmux app on your iPhone open this Mac's workspaces, terminals and agent chats while you are signed in with the same account.

Decides the size of a terminal while this Mac and a phone show it at once. A device that gets a larger terminal than it fits scrolls sideways or shows empty space; text never wraps wrong. Set the priority order in the cmux app on your iPhone.
The devices whose size a shared terminal takes first, highest first, when Terminal Size When Shared is Priority Order.
Even gives every pane in the column the same size after a split.
Off hides New Row and fits a column's existing rows into it without scrolling.
Moving the pointer onto a pane or scrolling over it focuses that pane. Off keeps focus where you type until you click. Momentum and the first second after typing never move focus.
Side-by-side panes that do not fit scroll sideways instead of shrinking, also in docked columns.

Command + Scroll moves columns and rows from anywhere, and a plain scroll always scrolls the pane under the pointer. Without a modifier, a sideways scroll moves columns unless the pane scrolls sideways itself, and rows scroll only over the gaps between them.
A web page that uses Command + Scroll itself, such as Figma or Excalidraw zooming, keeps it. Over any other page, Command + Scroll moves columns. Off, Command + Scroll always moves columns.
Web Pages Get Command + Scroll First
Open a Tab adds a tab to the focused pane. Split Automatically splits the largest pane, like New Pane (Auto Layout).
With Split Automatically, new browsers also get their own pane instead of a tab.
Where a link or file you open from a terminal, an agent chat, Home or a page appears. Split Right uses the pane on the right, or makes one.
Agent Chats keeps an agent chat as the main pane: links, files, subagents and side chats it opens appear as tabs in a column on its right, and closing that column gives the chat its full width back.
Where Cmd-N, the + button and the CLI put a new workspace in the sidebar. A workspace made in a group goes to the same place inside that group. Pinned workspaces stay above it.
Off: one list of workspaces, and a workspace on another computer names it under its title. On: a section per computer.
A workspace you have not named shows its front tab's name: a page's title, an agent chat's title, or a terminal's title or folder. Your own name always wins.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
A word that names a command by its action id ("vs": "splitRight"). Typing the whole word in the command palette puts that command first.
Commands shown first when the command palette opens, in this order, by action id.
Show chats stored on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
Find harness chat folders automatically. When off, only the listed folders are used.
Add absolute paths to harness data folders. Protected folders are refused. Your organization can add locked folders.
The picker lists these folders under Locations, after Home and Downloads. Use full paths or ~/ paths.
The Screenshots pane also shows the folders of screenshot apps it finds, such as CleanShot X, Shottr and Kap.
The Screenshots pane also shows the pictures and videos in these folders. Use full paths or ~/ paths.
What cmux does with workspaces you have not used for a while. Archived workspaces stay in their group, dimmed and last, and come back when you open them.
A workspace counts as idle when you have not opened it and nothing in it changed for this many days. Pinned workspaces, running commands and workspaces that need you never archive.
Frees the memory of workspaces you have not used for a while. Terminals and agents keep running; pages and chats come back where they were when you open the workspace.
A workspace hibernates when you have not opened it and nothing in it changed for this many minutes. Pinned workspaces, running commands and agents, and workspaces kept awake never hibernate.
When no window shows a space, its workspaces hibernate after this many idle minutes instead. Pinned workspaces, running commands and agents, and workspaces kept awake never hibernate.
Inbox lists what needs you first, with the task beside it. Changes apply at once.
Colors for terminals. cmux uses them too while App Theme is Match Terminal Theme. A space, workspace or terminal theme overrides it.
Colors for the window, sidebar, tabs and cmux's pages. Terminals keep the Terminal Theme. Every color meets WCAG AA contrast.
Your color changes to a theme, such as "Rose Pine/background": "#1f1d2e". The theme itself never changes; remove an entry to reset that color.
The color of selection, focus and the Send button. Theme Color takes the theme's own hue, such as Rose Pine's iris.
The color of selected text everywhere: terminals, Markdown, editors, the address bar and text fields. Unset, it is the terminal theme's selection color.
A public-domain painting behind the window material. Lower Opacity to reveal it. Attribution is linked above.
Choose a public-domain painting, your desktop wallpaper, or a macOS system wallpaper behind the window material.
How often a shuffled background turns to its next picture.
One background behind the whole window, or a copy in each pane. A pane's own background (right-click a pane) shows either way.
Draws windows in the plain theme color, without paintings, wallpapers or glass. Your background choices stay as they are and come back when you turn it off.
Applies Hue and Saturation to the window's tint. Off, they have no effect.
How much of the theme color covers the material behind the window.
Unset, the window follows Ghostty's background-opacity and background-blur.
How much more theme color covers a window while another one is in front. 0 keeps the same look.
The glass takes the colors of your desktop picture and follows it when the picture or Space changes.
How much of the desktop or wallpaper shows through the glass.
Shift the tint color around the hue wheel.
Increase or reduce the tint color intensity.
Row height, padding, corners, icons and text size together. Compact is the default.
Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.
Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.
None removes every border, hairline and separator in the app.
How the focused pane stands out: its border, subtler tabs in the other panes, both or neither.
How the other panes' tabs draw subtler when Focused Pane marks tabs: Fade dims them, Tonal steps their text down, Quiet keeps only a faint selected pill.
The look of the window: whether panes sit in one rounded card, and where lines are drawn. Separation, Sidebar Background and the sidebar border still win when you set them.
Splits, closes, moves, zooms, column scrolls and screen switches slide into place. Off: they change at once.
A new tab grows into its place in the tab bar. Off shows it there at once.
A new workspace row opens in the sidebar. Off shows it there at once.
None stops tabs, rows and panes exactly at their place. Subtle lets them settle with a small bounce.
How panes are told apart. None draws no border or divider at all; dragging between panes still resizes them. Default: dividers inside the curved main pane, borders otherwise.

Calm: nothing slides, springs or spins, hover cards stay closed and the pointer leaves no highlight on tabs, rows and buttons. Still: Calm, and every animation is instant. Your other motion and hover card settings come back when it is off.
Off turns every animation in cmux off: rows, tabs, panes, menus, cards, the agent cursor, spinners and cmux web pages change at once. On, the switches below choose area by area.
Rows and groups slide when they reorder, open, close, pin or move to the top, and the sidebar slides when it shows or hides. Off: they change at once.
Tabs grow, shrink and slide when they open, close, reorder or collapse into a group. Off: the tab bar changes at once.
Splits, closes, zooms, dividers, focus rings, drop zones and windows open, close and move with motion. Off: they change at once.
Menus, popovers, the command palette, sheets, toasts, notices, find bars and cards fade and slide in and out. Off: they show and hide at once.
Hover cards and tooltips fade and slide in. Off: they show and hide at once.
The Chief chat, its bubbles, the composer and the Home list move and fade. Off: they change at once.
The agent cursor glides between points and shows click ripples. Off: it jumps and shows no ripple.
Spinners turn, status dots pulse and attention flashes blink. Off: they show a still glyph.
Hover and press highlights, focus fades and theme color changes ease in. Off: they change at once.
Transitions and animations in cmux's own pages, such as agent chats, New Tab and Markdown. Off: they end at once. Websites are not changed.
How sidebar rows, tabs and panes show work in progress.
Static draws a still, distinct shape for each state. Reduce Motion always uses Static.
Three dots take the tab's icon place while an agent works.
A spinner takes a browser tab's icon place while its page loads.
A status that asks for a style (cmux status set --style) uses it.
A shell command that runs a while shows as busy.
Stage All and Revert All Bar
Web image sites can see your address and when you open a document. When off, each document asks before loading its web images.
The widest a line of text gets, in characters (30 to 1000). On a wider window the text stays centered with margins. Wide tables and code scroll sideways in their own box.
Text fills the whole pane instead of the text width.
The text size every markdown viewer opens at. Cmd-= and Cmd-- change it in one viewer; Cmd-0 goes back to this size.
The gap after each paragraph, as a share of the text size.
Code as a share of the text size. A monospaced font looks bigger than the text font at the same size, so code is a little smaller by default.
The font of code blocks and inline code. Empty uses the terminal font. The agent chat uses it too unless it has its own.
The widest the chat's column gets. On a wider pane the chat stays centered.
The chat fills the whole pane instead of the text width.
A small picture of the whole chat at its right edge, as in VS Code. Click or drag it to scroll.
The font of code in the chat. Empty uses the Markdown viewer's code font, then the terminal font.
Code as a share of the chat's text size. Empty uses the Markdown viewer's.
Where the Session Info panel opens at the right of the chat. Push narrows the chat beside it; Overlay lies over the chat.
Left puts it in a row below the tab row; Right keeps it in the header (or leads the tab-row tools); Off hides it.
What runs down the chat's edge: the rail, one tick per prompt; the full map, every message at its place with a box for what is on screen; or nothing.
How much of each turn a chat shows. Normal folds thinking and tool output; Thinking opens thinking; Verbose also opens tool output. A chat's ··· menu changes its own view.
The edge of the chat the prompt rail sits on, one tick per prompt. Right-click the rail to move it.
A monospaced font installed on this Mac.

Where a URL goes when a program in a terminal opens a browser, such as aws login or gh auth login: cmux, system, chrome, safari, arc, firefox, edge, brave, app:<name>, a profile after @ (chrome@Profile 1), or command:<command> to let your script decide. A BROWSER you set yourself wins.

Checked in order before the default; the first match wins. Write <match> -> <target>: caller:aws matches the program that opened the URL, and text, * wildcards or re: match the URL. Example: caller:gh github.com -> safari
Empty uses the terminal font size. Cmd-= and Cmd-- change it in one editor.
0 computes it from the font size. A value under 8 multiplies the font size.
Tab inserts spaces. Off inserts a tab character.
Tab size and spaces follow the file's own indentation.
Opt-Z turns it on and off.
Columns where a vertical line shows.
The lines that open the scopes around the top line stay at the top while you scroll.
Zoom with Command and the Scroll Wheel
The key you hold while you click to add a cursor.
Copy the Line When Nothing Is Selected
End Files with a Newline on Save
Runs the language's formatter when one is installed.
cmux reads that editor's settings and keybindings files and never changes them. A setting you make here wins.
Same as Main Pane gives the sidebar the main pane's background. Separate shades the sidebar darker than the main pane.
A line on the sidebar's edge. Off, the edge shows a line only while you hover or drag it.
How the sections above and below the workspace list draw.
The share of the sidebar the top sections fill before they scroll.
The share of the sidebar the bottom sections fill before they scroll.
Off: the top and bottom sections never scroll and the workspace list gets smaller.
On the New Tab page, the Threads and Console styles list every coding agent chat on this computer, newest first. Off, they show the recent chats only.
Show All Chats on New Tab
Lists a workspace that another workspace's agent started under it, and shows each row's pull requests and the first rows' Command-number keys.
A magnifying glass after the profile button searches workspaces, tabs, history, agent chats, settings and commands. Off, Search stays in the command palette.
A chevron beside the + in the sidebar's titlebar opens the New Workspace menu. Off, right-click the + for the same menu.
Each workspace is one line, like Claude's sidebar, and Command-Shift-[ and ] go to the previous or next workspace instead of the previous or next tab.
A group's colored name chip joins a thicker rail with a clipped corner, and the rail ends in a rounded cap, like Chrome's tab groups.
A press on a workspace row switches only when you release it, so you can hold and drag the row onto a pane's edge to show that workspace beside the current one. Workspaces on screen are highlighted.
The sidebar's edges stop fading and the whole list shows. It also hides the bottom profile and search bar. Off, the edges fade and the bar shows.

The sidebar's New Workspace button, spaces, profile button and Search button, and the sidebar button, Back and Forward above it, show only while the pointer is over the sidebar. Off, they always show.
Show Sidebar Controls Only on Hover
Workspace rows show only their icon, name and unread mark, and section titles become thin lines.
Rail shrinks the sidebar to a thin strip with a mark for each workspace. Point at the strip to open the full sidebar over your work.

Comfortable rows keep one line on taller rows with more space around them. Expanded rows show each workspace's status or folder under its name, how long ago it changed, and its pull request and computer.
Makes the sidebar's names, headers, icons and rows larger together. Larger matches the ChatGPT app's sidebar.
Workspace rows show a separate icon for working, waiting for input, error and done. Off, a row shows a spinner while it works and a blue dot when it is ready for you.
Workspace rows show when they last changed: a time today, else an age such as 3d. Off, rows show no times; the hover card still does.
Workspaces and groups draw their colors in the sidebar. Off, the sidebar draws no colors and keeps the colors you set.
How a workspace's color shows in the sidebar: a dot before its name, a bar down the row's edge, or the whole row filled with the color.
With workspaces on more than one computer, a workspace on another computer shows that computer's icon in its color. On, this Mac's workspaces show its icon too.
A collapsed group shows how many workspaces it holds after its name. Off, it shows only its loading spinner.
A collapsed group shows how many unread notifications its workspaces have. Off, it shows only its loading spinner.
Hides the chosen sections until the pointer is over the sidebar.
A "Did you know" card above the account button shows one cmux feature a day that you have not used yet. Each tip shows only once.
A bell at the top of the sidebar shows every agent chat on every machine, the ones waiting on you first, then finished, failed, working and idle.
The sidebar bell's state while the Priority view is on. Off, the sidebar is unchanged.
The window edge the sidebar sits on. On the right, the window buttons sit over the tab bar.
Where the spaces dots sit in the sidebar: under the window buttons or above the Settings row.
Always keeps the spaces shown, also when the sidebar's controls show only on hover. On Hover lets them hide with the other controls then.
Workspaces: Command-1 to 9 go to sidebar items and Control-1 to 9 to tabs. Tabs: Command-1 to 9 go to the focused pane's tabs and Control-1 to 9 to workspaces.
Every item: Home is Command-1, the App Store Command-2, the first workspace Command-3. Workspaces only: the first workspace is Command-1.
Goes to the last item, as in browsers, or to the ninth.
What Command-Control-] and Command-Control-[ step through.
Past the last item, the next item is the first again.
A card with details opens when the pointer rests on a workspace or a tab.
How long the pointer rests on a workspace or a tab before its card opens. While a card shows, the next one opens at once.
What a workspace's hover card shows: its history of prompts and waits, its details, or both.
How long the workspace has worked or waited, and how long its command has run.
Show Running Times in Workspace Cards
Each prompt you sent and when, in the card's history.
When an agent waited for your input or finished its turn, in the card's history.
The workspace's branch and pull request.
The ports the workspace listens on.
The most prompts, waits and finished turns a workspace's card lists. The list scrolls.
A summary card opens when the pointer rests on a workspace group's header.
A summary card opens when the pointer rests on a tab group's chip.
How long the pointer rests on a group before its summary card opens.
Which part of a group's card comes first.
The most members a group's card lists by name.
Show how many members work, wait, failed or have unread items.
Show the member count and the members' names.
Show the member that changed last, and when.
A player for what is playing, at the bottom of the sidebar.
Also show what plays in other apps, such as Spotify, Music or another browser. Off: only what plays in cmux.
Include Other Apps in Now Playing
A player for what is playing, on the New Tab page.
Show Now Playing on New Tab
Offer Picture in Picture for a web page's video in menus, the command palette and the media controls. A site's own video controls are not affected.
A headline over the composer that asks what to work on, with the project as a picker.
Ask What to Work On on New Tab
A card of this Mac and its recent projects over the composer.
Chats that need you, and New Terminal, New Browser Tab and New Chat.
Show Quick Actions on New Tab
Your recent chats under the composer. The palette finds any chat.
Show Recent Chats on New Tab
Dots under the page that switch its template.
Show Template Dots on New Tab
The current weather and today's high and low, for the city below or your time zone's city.
A city for the weather widget. Empty uses your time zone's city.
Your machines and whether each is online.
A quiet local time display beside the composer.
A small elapsed-time stopwatch beside the composer.
A time-of-day greeting such as Good afternoon.
Show Warm Greeting on New Tab
A bundled public-domain quote, changing daily.
Show Quote of the Day on New Tab
The order of the widgets on New Tab. Right-click New Tab and choose Edit New Tab to drag them.
Workspace, theme and color changes blend from the old colors to the new ones. Off: they change at once.
How long a color change takes. 0 changes colors at once.
How a color change moves over its duration. Spring uses Spring Response and Spring Damping; Custom uses the four Bezier values.
Seconds a spring color change takes to reach its new colors.
1 arrives smoothly with no overshoot. Above 1 is slower; below 1 arrives sooner.
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
A control point of the Custom (Bezier) curve, as in CSS cubic-bezier().
OKLab blends with even lightness. sRGB mixes the red, green and blue channels.
What color changes do while Reduce Motion is on in macOS.
The icon or emoji you chose for a workspace.
The terminal's title, which the shell or program sets.
The status agents and hooks report, one line each.
Set by a hook: cmux workspace status set ports <text>.
Set by a hook: cmux workspace status set pr <text>.
A progress bar under the row and the busy mark of running work.
A mark while an agent works in the workspace.
The newest line agents and scripts log: cmux workspace log append <text>.
The text of the workspace's newest unread notification.
The order of the shown items under the workspace name.
Buttons shown next to the address bar. The rest are in the More menu, where Show in Toolbar pins them back.
Browser tabs and cmux pages, such as History and Apps, open in this engine.

Sites that always open in one engine: a site, such as spotify.com, and chromium or webkit. Spotify, Netflix and other protected media sites open in WebKit, because their media does not play in Chromium.
An address such as https://example.com. Empty opens a blank page.
A row of bookmarks under each browser toolbar.

Offers to bring bookmarks, history, passwords and sign-ins over from other browsers: Import from Browser in the File menu and the palette, and the import cards in Settings. Off hides them and nothing imports by itself. Data already imported stays.
Browser tabs offer to import cookies from your other browsers, so you stay signed in. Nothing imports until you click Import. Don't Show Again on the banner turns this off.
When an agent drives a browser tab, show its cursor, clicks and typed keys on the page. Password fields show dots.

How an agent moves the pointer in browser tabs. Human moves along a curved path and rests before each click, as a person does, so pages see hover and timing like a person's. Instant jumps to the target and clicks at once.
The longest time one agent pointer move takes with human motion. Short moves take less.
The full uBlock Origin blocks ads and trackers in Chromium tabs. Takes effect after cmux restarts.
Frees memory; history and position are kept. Also accepts a number from 1 to 1440 in a raw profile.
Saves power: a hidden Chromium tab stops running until you show it. Pinned tabs and Never Hibernate hosts stay awake. Also accepts a number from 5 to 3600 in a raw profile.
Tabs on each side of the shown tab stay loaded and running, so switching to them is instant. 0 turns it off. Memory pressure and Low Power Mode turn it off.
Open localhost on the Workspace's Machine
The address bar searches here and asks it for suggestions.
Used when Search Engine is Custom. Put {searchTerms} where the typed text goes.
Optional. Answers in the OpenSearch suggestions format, with {searchTerms} for the typed text.
Sends what you type to the search engine for suggestions. Never addresses, files or local hosts.
Completes a site you typed before or visit often.
Shows the answer to arithmetic you type. Return copies it.
Shows the whole address, with https:// and www., when you are not editing it.
The material of the address bar. Transparent draws no fill. Clear glass shows more of what is behind it. Off uses the flat theme color.
The color over the glass, from the terminal theme. Accent is the theme's own accent color, or gray when the theme has none.
Match Theme uses the standard bar radius. Capsule rounds the ends fully. Also accepts a number from 0 to 16 in a raw profile.
A soft shadow under the glass address bar.
How much the address bar covers a see-through window. At 0 it is as see-through as the window, but never so clear that its text stops being readable.
Match Density follows the density. The bar always grows to fit its text. Also accepts a number from 20 to 56 in a raw profile.
The size of the address and the suggestions. Match Density follows the density. Also accepts a number from 10 to 24 in a raw profile.
In Chromium tabs, Download keeps Chrome's default.
In Chromium tabs, Download keeps Chrome's default.
Chromium tabs use the Command-Click setting.
When off, cmux opens no browser tabs for web pages and every link opens in your default browser.
When off, links you click in terminals, agent chats, Home and cmux pages open in your default browser. Shift-Command-click opens a link in the other browser.

Sign-in and device-code pages, such as GitHub's device page or a page gh, aws or an agent opens to sign in, open in a cmux browser tab even when other links open in your default browser. URLs to Always Open Externally still win.
Open Sign-In Pages in cmux Browser
When off, links clicked in terminal output open in your default browser.
Open Terminal Links in cmux Browser
Only these hosts open in cmux, such as example.com or *.example.com. Empty opens every host in cmux.
Hosts to Open in Embedded Browser
Links that match open in your default browser. Text matches anywhere in the URL, * and ? are wildcards, and re: starts a regular expression.
The app Open in Text Editor uses for a path: an app name, a bundle ID or the path of an app. Empty uses the app that opens source code.
A browser tab asks to save a sign-in you submit. Tabs an agent drives never ask.
Offers a generated password when a site asks for a new one, and saves it.
Lets the Passwords page write every saved password to a plain-text CSV file, after you confirm with Touch ID or your password.
When a site emails you a code or link, its tab offers it. Only on the sender's own site, never filled without your click, and never stored.

Direct messages and group chats use cmux Cloud by default. A self-hosted server is reached over Tailscale by its MagicDNS name, for example http://mini.tail1234.ts.net:7320. No password is sent: the server knows you by your Tailscale login. Also accepts a dictionary {"selfHosted": "http(s)://host[:port]"} in a raw profile.
iMessage shows your messages in blue and the Chief's in gray. Theme uses your theme's accent and surface colors.
Every chat starts with these colors. Right-click a chat and choose Chat Colors to set its own. Unset text colors are picked to stay readable.
Every chat starts with these colors. Right-click a chat and choose Chat Colors to set its own. Unset text colors are picked to stay readable.
Every chat starts with these colors. Right-click a chat and choose Chat Colors to set its own. Unset text colors are picked to stay readable.
Every chat starts with these colors. Right-click a chat and choose Chat Colors to set its own. Unset text colors are picked to stay readable.
When off, location data is removed from photos and videos before they are attached.
Keep Location in Photos and Videos
Show Channels below Home in the sidebar. You can also turn it on or off from the command palette.
A small Chief floats over every app and shows agent events above it. Drag it anywhere; click it to message the Chief or reply to a session. While it shows, ⌃⌥⌘C opens its reply box from any app.
Which Chief Home opens. Auto uses this Mac's Chief while it runs here, else the Hosted Chief in the cloud.

A reaction you put on a Chief message can start a turn when it asks for one, such as a question mark on a question or a thumbs down on a plan. A cheap model decides first, so a reaction that needs no answer never shows the typing dots. Off, reactions are only noted.
The agent harness the reaction classifier runs on, for example claude or codex. Empty uses the Chief's Claude route.
The model that decides whether a reaction starts a turn. Claude Haiku by default: it is fast and cheap.
What the classifier is told when it decides. Empty uses the built-in instructions.

The Chief picks the agent each subagent runs on, such as Codex for long coding work and Claude for writing and UI, even when the Chief itself runs on another. Off, subagents run on the Chief's own agent.
Route Subagents to the Best Agent
Used when a source clears after a timeout.
No banners or sounds between these times.
A pane typed into this recently is marked read at once. 0 turns it off.
cmux status run notifies when the command took at least this long.
Notify Even When the Terminal Is Visible
When a notification alerts while cmux isn't the active app.
Whether a banner shows what the agent said, or only where and what state.
Notifications from agents and cmux notify go to your cmux account's feed and can reach your iPhone.
Copy Agent Notifications to the Feed
Notifications that programs send through the terminal can contain secrets. Off sends nothing to your cmux account.
Copy Terminal Notifications to the Feed
Each request's tool and command summary goes to your own cmux feed, so your iPhone can answer it.
Send Agent Permission Requests to the Feed
Ring an agent chat's pane when its turn ends, until you click or type in it.
Clicking an unread pane, typing in it or jumping to it flashes its ring as it goes.
A notification moves its workspace to the top of the unpinned rows, unless you are looking at its pane.
Move the Workspace to the Top
Workspace ids whose notifications are silent. Mute a workspace from its sidebar row menu.
Sounds cmux plays itself. A banner's default sound follows the system alert volume.
Many notifications at once sound once. An agent asking for input still sounds. 0 turns it off.
Sounds per workspace id. Set one from the workspace's sidebar menu.
Sounds per group id or name. Set one from the group's sidebar menu.
Sounds per agent kind, such as claude or codex.
Unfinished surfaces, such as the agent session's coverage label and Pull requests view.
Show Home as a full page instead of a workspace with the Chief docked on the left. Takes effect after cmux restarts.
An unofficial room where you talk with people and Chief. While a room is open, cmux transcribes your mic and reads your screen's text on this Mac, then sends that text to the room.
The room's web address. Empty uses the room server on this Mac.
Add Device shows a line to paste on any Mac or Linux computer; it joins your team's machines. Screen sharing and control stay off until that machine allows them.
Join Any Machine with One Line
Uses your gh login to read notifications and review requests on this Mac. Sign in with gh auth login first.
Seconds between GitHub refreshes. Refresh in the Inbox runs immediately.
What a file link in a reply does when the file is outside the chat's folders. Keys and .env files never open.
A web image loads from its site, which then sees that you read the reply.
A badge in the chat header counts what your agents wait on; a click lists every ask with its answers. New agent tabs.
The card that lists a turn's edited files, with Undo and View changes.
The ring beside the model that fills as the chat uses its context window.
The microphone beside Send in every composer, including the New Tab page.
Underlines misspellings and offers system suggestions in the composer.
How pictures and files show in the composer and in sent messages. Inline puts each one in the text where you added it; Strip shows them in a row. The message and its order stay the same.
When off, sending while you are reading up keeps your place and shows new messages below.
Scroll to Bottom When I Send
Shows a warning when a remote machine is at its CPU or memory budget in the Computer menu.
Where a new chat runs. Cloud starts it on your own Cloud machine, with your project copied there. The new chat's composer can change it for that chat.
The display size for agent chat. Cmd-0 resets it.
What a new chat may do without asking. A mode you pick in a chat applies to that chat only.
The model a new chat on the cmux model router starts on. A model you pick in a chat applies to that chat only.

Nightly builds send a daily report of hangs and slow frames: call stacks of cmux and macOS code, timings, your app and macOS versions, your Mac's chip and memory size, and rounded counts of open windows and tabs. It never includes file names, web addresses, terminal text, names or anything you type. View Hang Report shows exactly what is sent.
While a Mac Screen tab has the keyboard, shortcuts like ⌘Tab, ⌘Space, Mission Control and ⌘Q go to the other Mac. Needs Accessibility.
Send System Shortcuts to the Remote Mac
Mac Screen tabs connect through the TURN relay only, never directly, to check the relay path. Tabs that are connected reconnect.
Overrides the device hub this build signs its devices in to, for Mac Screen sharing between your devices. Leave it empty to use the built-in hub.
Adds Customize Menu… to the end of every right-click menu.
Team enrollment token from the cmux dashboard. Signed-in users in a verified domain of the team join it; the token alone never grants membership.
Team id (team_...) that manages this device.
Refuse sign-in to any team other than ManagedTeam on this device.
Features to turn off: their UI, actions and host operations are removed.
Oldest cmux version allowed to sign in, for example 1.2.0.
Turn off automatic updates (also honored in the legacy com.cmuxterm.app domain).
Turn off anonymous telemetry, crash reports included, whatever the user chose (also honored in the legacy com.cmuxterm.app domain).
